draft.title: Maxwell-Boltzmann distributions
card: Particles in a gas or liquid do not all have the same energy. A Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution is a graph of this spread of energies.
The vertical axis shows the number of particles. The horizontal axis shows their energy. The area under the curve is the total number of particles.
The activation energy is marked as a line on the energy axis. Only particles to the right of that line have enough energy to react in a collision.
At a higher temperature the curve flattens and shifts right. The peak is lower and more particles lie past the activation energy.
draft.remember: Higher temperature moves the curve right, so more particles pass the activation energy.

a.q: On a Maxwell-Boltzmann graph, which particles have enough energy to react?
opts: Those to the right of the activation energy line
Those to the left of the activation energy line
Those at the peak of the curve
Those under the whole area of the curve
a.why: Particles with energy at or above the activation energy lie to its right on the energy axis. The peak shows the most common energy, which is usually below the activation energy.
a.clue: Higher energy is further along the horizontal axis.

b.q: A solution of reactants in Geelong is warmed by 10 degrees Celsius. How does its Maxwell-Boltzmann curve change, and why does this matter for the rate?
opts: It shifts right, so more particles pass the activation energy
It shifts right, so the activation energy line moves left
It shifts left, so more particles pass the activation energy
It stays still, but the number of particles under it rises
b.why: Warming moves the curve right and flattens it, so a larger share of particles lie past the activation energy. The activation energy itself does not change with temperature, and the area under the curve stays the same.
b.clue: The activation energy line stays where it is.
